paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption: Predicting narrative frames using oracle (human-annotated) and noisy (predicted) labels for their , , , and ; the results are macro-averaged F1.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the macro-averaged F1 scores for three different large language models—Gemini, GPT4o, and Sonnet—when evaluated using three distinct prompting strategies: “Basic prompt” (dark blue), “Structured prompt + oracle” (orange), and “Structured prompt + predicted” (dark green). The horizontal axis presents the three models in alphabetical order, while the vertical axis represents the F1 score, scaled linearly from 0 to 0.7, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. For each model, three bars are grouped side-by-side, with the “Basic prompt” bar consistently being the shortest, the “Structured prompt + oracle” bar being the tallest, and the “Structured prompt + predicted” bar falling in between. Specifically, for Gemini, the scores are approximately 0.32 (Basic), 0.61 (Structured + oracle), and 0.35 (Structured + predicted). For GPT4o, the scores are approximately 0.25 (Basic), 0.58 (Structured + oracle), and 0.47 (Structured + predicted). For Sonnet, the scores are approximately 0.33 (Basic), 0.52 (Structured + oracle), and 0.42 (Structured + predicted). The bars are not sorted by value, and no visual emphasis such as shading or outlines is applied to any particular bar.
